html:
The Rwandan genocide was the killing of between about half a million and 800,000 or more people, most of them Tutsi, by Hutu extremists in Rwanda in about one hundred days from April to July 1994.

It began the night after President Habyarimana's plane was shot down. Soldiers, militias and ordinary people killed at roadblocks, in homes and in churches, using lists, radio calls and identity cards. Moderate Hutu were killed too. A small United Nations force was cut back.

It ended when the Rwandan Patriotic Front took the country. About two million Hutu fled, most into Zaire, starting the refugee crisis and the Congo wars. The international tribunal at Arusha and the local gacaca courts tried the killers, and the failure to act shaped the later doctrine of a responsibility to protect.
sum: The Rwandan genocide was the killing of between about half a million and 800,000 or more people, most of them Tutsi, by Hutu extremists in Rwanda in about one hundred days from April to July 1994.
